transcript:
Meeting header: Northforge Pilot - Week 3 Compliance Touchpoint
Date/Time: 2025-07-22 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Dana Lee (Northforge - Head ML), Omar Ruiz (Northforge - Security), Priya Shah (Northforge - VP Product)
Shared: security-questionnaire_v2.pdf (Redwood), pilot-pricing-v2.xlsx (Redwood)

[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick check — we've got about 45 minutes, main agenda is SSO, audit logs, retention and SOC 2 artifacts, does that look right?
[00:12] Dana: yup that works, wanting to make sure we can get the audit outputs we need before the exec steering next week.
[00:18] Omar: also need to confirm SAML flow with our Okta setup and how long logs stick around — security wants 90 days as baseline.
[00:25] Marcus: great, I can run through how Redwood currently surfaces audit logs and what options we have for retention and redaction.
[00:31] Priya: and also curious about scope of SOC 2 — do we get the actual report or just an attestation?

[00:40] Marcus: quick caveat, i'll try to not go too infra-deep right away. So audit logs today include request metadata, model id, route, timestamps, and hashed user identifiers by default. We can export as newline-delimited JSON or CSV. (uhm) There are two paths — short-term retention on hosted pilot (30 days), or extended retention via log-persistence add-on which keeps for 90/180 days.
[01:05] Omar: when you say hashed user identifiers, is that reversible? We need non-reversible hashed IDs for compliance.
[01:12] Marcus: right, we use a one-way HMAC with customer-specific salt for pilot exports — not reversible. I'll include the hash algorithm and sample in the export.
[01:22] Dana: will the export include prompt/response content? We were hoping to avoid storing full prompt text for PII reasons.
[01:29] Marcus: good question. Default export contains request metadata and timestamps; content is configurable. For pilot we can turn on content capture, but we also support redaction (regex rules) and automatic PII masking on ingest. For your use case we recommend enabling metadata-only export plus explicit redaction rules for named fields.
[01:48] Omar: can that redaction be applied retroactively to already-captured items?
[01:52] Marcus: retroactive redaction is limited — we can run backfills but best practice is to set rules at ingest. For the pilot we can run a backfill as a one-off; Marcus: (laugh) excuse me, i mean we can schedule that with ops.
[02:04] Avery: quick follow — Priya raised SOC 2 question. Lina, do you want to cover what Redwood can share?
[02:10] Lina: sure — Redwood can share our SOC 2 Type II report under NDA, plus a controls matrix mapping. For pilot customers we typically provide the cert, evidence mapping, and a short security whitepaper. For anything customer-specific we can provide architecture diagrams and KMS integration docs.
[02:28] Priya: is the SOC 2 scope covering private deployments and the hosted offering both?
[02:33] Lina: SOC 2 cert covers our hosted control plane and hosted inference clusters we manage; private (VPC / on-prem) has a different control boundary — we provide guidance and runbooks, but the customer maintains some controls. That said, we have documentation showing how to meet SOC 2 equivalence with private deploys.
[02:48] Omar: KMS — we need details on customer-managed keys, HSM support, and whether keys can stay in our KMS.
[02:55] Marcus: we offer KMS integrations — you can bring-your-own KMS or use our managed keys with envelope encryption. HSM-backed KMS supported for private deployments; for hosted there are vetted KMS providers. We'll send exact config snippets.
[03:06] Dana: one operational concern — latency impact if we enable encryption-at-rest with customer KMS?
[03:10] Marcus: negligible for token-level operations; the main overhead is during model load/secret negotiation; typical impact is a few ms on startup but not on steady-state token throughput.
[03:20] Priya: ok thanks. Another question on SSO — we use Okta, and we'd like SAML-based SCIM provisioning. Does Redwood support SCIM for user provisioning and SAML SSO?
[03:30] Avery: yes, we support SAML SSO (IdP-initiated and SP-initiated) and SCIM for provisioning. We can provide metadata and a test connector. Marcus: we usually ask for a test user and metadata during pilot to validate.
[03:40] Omar: what's the expected lead time to validate SSO? We have a security gating process that takes a few days.
[03:44] Marcus: in practice we validate in 1-2 business days if credentials and metadata are provided; test user helps speed it up.
[03:50] Dana: can roles map to RBAC within Redwood? We want to map Okta groups to editor/viewer roles.
[03:55] Marcus: yes — group mapping to RBAC is supported; we'll include a sample role mapping file.
[04:01] Priya: about logs again — are there live-tail capabilities or only exports?
[04:05] Marcus: console has live-tail for admins with filters; exports are for long-term storage / SIEM ingestion. We can also push to your Splunk/Datadog via forwarding.
[04:14] Omar: Splunk forwarder would be ideal. Do you have an example config?
[04:18] Marcus: yes — i'll attach a sample HEC config and a mini runbook for TLS certs.
[04:23] Avery: (brief) On the pilot pricing side, if you opt for 90-day retention there is a modest add-on — i'll send a revised sheet after the call.
[04:31] Dana: perfect. For the SOC 2 report we will need the report and evidence mapping by next Wednesday for the steering committee.
[04:37] Lina: we can provide the report under NDA; Avery will put that in motion.
[04:41] Omar: one more — data residency: Northforge requires EU residency for certain datasets. How do you handle region pinning?
[04:49] Marcus: region pinning is available — we can route inference to eu-west and store logs in eu region. For hosted it's an option; private deploy is naturally inside your region.
[04:59] Priya: do you support data residency for audit logs too?
[05:02] Marcus: yes, logs can be region-constrained. We'll document the storage location per export.
[05:08] Dana: ok next steps then?
[05:11] Avery: recap: Marcus will produce anonymized audit export and HMAC details, Lina/Avery will share SOC2 and controls matrix under NDA, Avery will update pilot pricing for 90-day retention, Lina will schedule a technical deep dive for private/KMS. Customer to confirm Okta metadata and identify test user.
[05:25] Priya: sounds good, thanks all.
[05:28] Omar: quick note, i'll send a short list of PII fields we want redacted.
[05:32] Marcus: got it, we'll include a sample redaction rule set.
[05:35] Avery: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts — expect the audit export link by Sunday.
[05:40] Meeting end.
